title: Tech Radar 2026: Pragmatic Evaluation of Adopting Rust in Enterprise Backend Systems
summary: Multi-dimensional analysis on memory safety, CPU throughput, developer learning curve, and lessons learned from deploying Rust in production microservices.
author: Huỳnh Nhật Tân

sections.introduction: In the 2026 technology landscape, Rust has emerged as a premier language for critical infrastructure. This article shares practical engineering insights from prototyping and shipping a high-throughput microservice in Rust (Actix-web / Tokio) in enterprise production.
sections.multi-dimensional-evaluation:
Comprehensive evaluation across core criteria:

  • Strengths: Memory safety without Garbage Collection overhead, remarkably low memory footprint (< 15MB for active web instances), and nearly zero runtime bugs due to the expressive type system and borrow checker.
  • Challenges: Longer compilation times, higher hiring and training costs, and fewer turnkey enterprise ORM integrations compared to mature Java or Go ecosystems.
sections.case-study-experience: Rewrote a high-volume JWT token verification and rate-limiting gateway from Node.js to Rust. Outcome: p99 latency dropped from 18ms to 1.2ms, CPU utilization reduced by 75%, and GC latency jitter was completely eliminated.
sections.actionable-recommendations: Recommendation: Avoid wholesale rewrites. Begin adoption on performance-sensitive edge proxies, cryptographic engines, or CPU-intensive data pipelines before expanding to team-wide initiatives.
sections.open-questions-discussion: Will the rise of Java Virtual Threads and Go concurrency diminish the performance advantage of Rust for standard CRUD web backends? We invite your thoughts.

title: Scaling ERP Reporting Portal for 1,000+ Concurrent Users with Redis & Node.js
summary: Heavy reporting query caching techniques, asynchronous batch processing, and modular interface design strategies.
author: Huỳnh Nhật Tân

sections.context-problem: During end-of-month financial closing periods, over 1,000 enterprise clients simultaneously requested ledger balance and inventory reports. The relational database suffered severe I/O bottlenecks, causing API response times to exceed 12 seconds.
sections.system-requirements:
• Throughput & Latency: Serve 1,000+ concurrent enterprise users while keeping 95th percentile API response times under 800ms.
  • Data Freshness: Financial reports must reflect ledger changes within 5 minutes.
sections.architecture-design:
Layered caching and asynchronous worker architecture:

  • Multi-Level Caching: Redis Cluster storing serialized JSON aggregates with 5-minute TTLs and proactive cache warm-up cron jobs.
  • Asynchronous Export Queue: Large Excel/PDF reporting jobs offloaded to background BullMQ workers, delivering download URLs via WebSocket on completion.
sections.trade-offs-analysis:
Balancing Immediate Consistency vs High Availability:

  • Accepted a 5-minute data staleness window on cached reporting views in exchange for an 85% reduction in direct database query load.
  • Implemented event-driven cache invalidation when high-priority ledger settlements occurred.
sections.lessons-best-practices: Implement distributed Mutex Locks (Redlock) to prevent Cache Stampedes and Cache Avalanches when hot cache keys expire under heavy traffic spikes.

title: Building Real-time Financial Ledger Aggregation Pipeline with ClickHouse for Millions of Transactions
summary: Leveraging ClickHouse columnar storage and SummingMergeTree engines to calculate ledger reconciliation balances in under 50ms.
author: Huỳnh Nhật Tân

sections.business-data-requirements: The financial department required instantaneous balance sheet analysis across 50+ million monthly retail transactions. PostgreSQL GROUP BY and SUM queries took over 25 seconds per chart refresh.
sections.data-modeling:
Optimized table schema in ClickHouse:

  • SummingMergeTree Engine: Automatically aggregates debit/credit amounts during background merge passes, eliminating 90% of row scans during query time.
  • Partitioning: Monthly partitioning with toYYYYMM(transaction_date) and primary key ordering by (account_id, currency, transaction_date).
sections.pipeline-construction:
Streaming pipeline architecture:

  • Real-time event streaming from Kafka via ClickHouse Kafka Engine tables.
  • Direct ingestion and data transformation via Materialized Views without requiring intermediate worker application layers.
sections.testing-optimization: Performance benchmarks across 100 million ledger rows: Query execution dropped from 28 seconds to 38ms. Achieved a 6.5x data compression ratio over raw SSD disk usage.
sections.summary-recommendations: ClickHouse is exceptionally suited for high-volume financial analytics. Recommendation: Avoid single-row inserts; always batch writes between 10,000 and 100,000 records.

title: Zero-Downtime Blue-Green Deployments with Docker Compose & Nginx Reverse Proxy
summary: Production release architecture using alternating environments and automated Nginx upstream switching via shell scripts.
author: Huỳnh Nhật Tân

sections.article-objectives: Implement zero-downtime release automation for medium-scale enterprise web services using Blue-Green deployments with instant rollback safety.
sections.architecture-principles:
Two identical containerized environments:

  • Blue (Live): Actively serving production traffic on port 8081.
  • Green (Idle): Receives new version releases on port 8082, executes migrations, and validates smoke tests.
  • Nginx Proxy: Routes traffic and issues nginx -s reload for seamless upstream switching.
sections.step-by-step-setup:
Deployment pipeline stages:

  • Step 1: Pull updated Docker image and spin up the idle environment (Green).
  • Step 2: Execute health check validation on /healthz until HTTP 200 is verified.
  • Step 3: Atomically update Nginx upstream configuration and execute reload.
  • Step 4: Gracefully stop the previous environment after a 60-second in-flight draining window.
sections.troubleshooting-pitfalls:
• Database Schema Incompatibility: Occurs when migrations remove columns still read by the old version. Solve via the Expand and Contract pattern.
  • Dropped TCP Connections: Ensure Nginx is reloaded with HUP signal so old worker processes finish existing requests before terminating.
sections.evaluation-scaling: Eliminated midnight maintenance windows, allowing continuous deployments 5-10 times daily with confidence and zero user disruption.
